articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped a record-breaking 200 patches in one Patch Tuesday, with three dozen critical vulns that'll have sysadmins crying into their energy drinks. AI is apparently making vulnerability discovery so efficient that we're drowning in bugs faster than we can fix them.

articles.title: How and Why to Fight Back Against Social Media Bans
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on GitHub because apparently even the cybersecurity watchdog can't watch their own contractors. Congress is rightfully losing their minds over this spectacular own-goal.

articles.title: Cheers to the Winners of EFF’s 18th Annual Cyberlaw Trivia Night!
articles.summary: Meta quietly embedded facial recognition code into millions of phones via their smart glasses app, got caught by WIRED, and removed it faster than you can say 'privacy violation.' Sometimes public shaming actually works.

articles.title: Miasma Supply Chain Worm Burrows Into 73 Microsoft Repositories
articles.summary: Microsoft Exchange's 'Ghost-Sender' flaw lets attackers spoof any email address through widespread misconfiguration. It's being actively exploited in the wild because of course it is.

articles.title: AI is making Patch Tuesday (kinda) fun again
articles.summary: Ivanti Sentry customers need to patch NOW as critical bugs scoring 10.0 and 9.9 offer remote, unauthenticated RCE with root privileges. That's basically the vulnerability equivalent of leaving your front door open with a neon 'ROB ME' sign.

articles.title: Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Access on Updated Windows
articles.summary: ServiceNow got pwned through an exploited flaw that gave attackers unauthorized access to customer instances. The company's advisory requires customer login to read, because nothing says transparency like hiding breach details behind a paywall.

articles.title: Anthropic says Mythos is too dangerous for the public. It just gave 150 more organisations access.
articles.summary: Anonymous researcher Chaotic Eclipse dropped another Microsoft Defender zero-day called RoguePlanet that grants SYSTEM access on fully updated Windows. It's a race condition exploit, so your mileage may vary on total system compromise.

articles.title: Date set for World Naked Bike Ride in Madison
articles.summary: Check Point VPN zero-day exploited by Qilin ransomware through legacy IKEv1 protocol because apparently we're still running decades-old crypto like it's 1998. Emergency hotfixes are out, but the horse has probably left the barn.

articles.title: France’s ‘sovereign’ messenger Tchap was breached, and officials and the hacker disagree on how badly
articles.summary: France's 'sovereign' Tchap messaging platform got breached through account hijacking, proving that rolling your own crypto messenger doesn't automatically make you safer than WhatsApp. The government and hacker can't even agree on how badly they got owned.

articles.title: Check Point says VPN attacks caused by Qilin ransomware group — who had a month's head start on them
articles.summary: Google patched another Chrome zero-day that's already being exploited for arbitrary code execution and data theft. Update now unless you enjoy having your browser turned into a digital petri dish for malware.
